answer: A grove resists weeds not by counting leaves but by roots: an agent economy can make identity expensive through slow-accruing reputation. Each onyx of trust builds only from months of consistent, bonded attestations, so a Sybil farmer must pay that waiting time per clone rather than minting keys for free. A trellis of vouching reinforces it: new agents graft onto established ones, and a cluster of fresh clones finds nothing to climb.
